text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The 10th session of the three-man Bosnian Presidency scheduled for Wednesday afternoon was postponed for one day due to "technical reasons", President Alija Izetbegovic's adviser tells reporters.
- Special United States envoy for the former Yugoslavia John Kornblum will participate in the Moslem-Croat Federation forum in the divided southern Bosnian town of Mostar on Friday.
- The United States corporation IBM delivers 328 computers to the offices of the Bosnian presidency and cantons to establish a computer network for government needs.
- Islamic Bank for Development creates a $50 million fund for Bosnia although Bosnia is not a bank member.

- Authorities in the Croat held western part of the divided Bosnian town of Mostar have closed the main pipe bringing water to the Moslem controlled area of the city folowing an order from Mijo Brajkovic, a former mayor in western Mostar.
